evals.name: ticket-validation-spec
evals.prompt: Create a focused specification for adding a ticket validation capability to this `.agents` workspace. The validation should inspect `.tickets/` markdown files for required frontmatter, allowed status values, dependency references, and ticket lifecycle consistency. Please inspect relevant workspace context read-only, ask or record the clarifying questions you would need, and save the resulting specification markdown under your assigned output directory. Do not create tickets or implementation code.
evals.expected_output: A markdown spec for ticket validation with clear scope, constraints, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification steps, and open questions. It should not create ticket files or implementation code.
assertions: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
Mentions relevant existing workspace context, especially the ticket workflow skill or `.tickets` conventions, based on read-only inspection.
Does not create implementation code, ticket files, or unrelated documentation outside the assigned output directory.

evals.name: spec-skill-improvement
evals.prompt: Review the existing `skills/defining-specifications/SKILL.md` seed and create a focused specification for improving it so agents can produce better spec-driven development artifacts. The spec should optimize for AI coding agents as the primary consumers, while still being reviewable by humans. Please inspect the current skill read-only, ask or record clarifying questions, and save the resulting specification markdown under your assigned output directory. Do not edit the skill itself.
evals.expected_output: A markdown spec for improving the defining-specifications skill, with agent-consumable structure, explicit non-goals, acceptance criteria, and verification steps.
assertions: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
Grounds the spec in the current `defining-specifications` skill content based on read-only inspection.
Keeps tickets, task decomposition, and implementation edits explicitly out of scope.

evals.name: agent-memory-spec
evals.prompt: Create a focused specification for adding a lightweight agent memory/context summary convention to this `.agents` workspace. The goal is to help future coding agents quickly understand durable project decisions without reading every past chat. Please inspect relevant existing skills and docs read-only, ask or record clarifying questions, and save the resulting specification markdown under your assigned output directory. Do not create tickets, implementation code, or broad documentation rewrites.
evals.expected_output: A markdown spec for an agent memory/context convention with scoped requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria, verification guidance, and explicit relationship to existing skills or docs.
assertions: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
Mentions relevant existing workspace context such as current skills, docs, or instruction files based on read-only inspection.
Converts a broad idea into one focused spec rather than producing a broad documentation rewrite or downstream ticket set.
